Hankinta sisältää tilaturvallisuusjärjestelmien ja niiden hallinta-alustan toimittamisen ja käyttöönoton käyttökuntoon saakka, sekä korjaus-, huolto- ja ylläpitopalvelut. description: The purpose of this amendment is to extend the deadline for submission of proposals to 02 October 2026, to include clauses 52.233-1, 52.233-3, and 252.243-7002, and to provide revisions to the RFP in response to RFIs received. All amended language within the solicitation will be bolded and highlighted where possible for visibility......................................................................................................................PROJECT TITLE: RYGGE MUNITIONS STORAGE AREA EXPANSIONPROJECT LOCATION: RYGGE, NORWAYTHIS CONSTRUCTION PROJECT WILL BE A COMPETITIVE, FIRM-FIXED PRICE DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONTRACT PROCURED VIA A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR PARTS 15 AND 36 AND THE TRADEOFF SOURCE SELECTION PROCESS. THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED (FULL-AND-OPEN COMPETITION) RFP WITH A BRAND-NAME REQUIREMENT UNDER NAICS CODE 236220. THE SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD FOR THIS NAICS CODE IS $45,000,000.00.The United States Corps of Engineers Europe District has a requirement on behalf of the United States Air Force (USAF) to build and extend the munitions storage area (MSA) on Rygge Air Station in support of USAF contingency operations in Norway. The project includes the construction of 20 ammunition storage magazines (earth-covered magazines, or ECMs) to accommodate a total Net Explosive Weight (NEW) of 3,000,000 pounds. A standard ammunition storage magazine design which supports up to a maximum capacity of 165,000 pounds NEW will be used for all 20 magazine/bunkers. Supporting facilities include one concrete munitions assembly pad, one stuff on-off pad, gravel roads, bermed areas, lighting, security fencing surmounted by barbed wire, and utility connections for communications and electrical. This project is in direct support of the European Deterrence Initiative (EDI) and the Supplementary Defense Cooperation Agreement (SDCA) between the United States and the Government of Norway, and is intended to be compatible with applicable NATO, DoD, Air Force, and host-nation design standards.

title: Social and emotional robot
description: Social and emotional robot The procurement consists of one (1) programmable and interactive social and emotional humanoid/service robot. The total value of the procurement shall not exceed EUR 75,000 (VAT 0%). The robot shall be designed for safe indoor operation and human interaction. It must support Finnish-language communication and be capable of facilitating social interaction, autonomous activities, emotional engagement, and the safe handling of objects. The robot must be suitable for educational, guidance, rehabilitation, and student support environments. The primary purpose of the procurement is to support Care Assistant Education by providing students with hands-on experience in healthcare and welfare technologies, social robotics, communication, guidance, and technology-assisted care. The robot will also be used in simulation-based learning and to familiarise students with technologies commonly encountered in modern working life. In addition, the robot will be available for multidisciplinary use across the contracting authority's educational programmes and support services. It will function as a shared pedagogical resource that promotes communication, participation, digital skills, and familiarity with emerging technologies. The robot may be used in various educational and operational roles, including learning support, interactive communication, visitor guidance, information sharing, wellbeing reminders, event reception, and customer interaction training. The contracting authority seeks a versatile, user-friendly, and pedagogically effective solution that supports inclusive learning environments and provides long-term value across multiple user groups and educational contexts.,

title: XR-pohjaisen oppimisratkaisun yhteiskehittäminen ja toteutus matkailualan ammatilliseen koulutukseen
description: XR-pohjaisen oppimisratkaisun yhteiskehittäminen ja toteutus matkailualan ammatilliseen koulutukseen 1. Hankinnan tavoite ja kohde Hankinnan kohteena on matkailualan toisen asteen ammatilliseen koulutukseen tarkoitetun pelillisen simulaatio- tai XR-pohjaisen oppimisratkaisun yhteiskehittäminen ja toteuttaminen. Ratkaisun tulee soveltua tarkoituksenmukaisilta osin myös ammattikorkeakouluopetukseen. Hankinta toteutetaan osana Euroopan unionin osarahoittamaa Immersiivisen oppimisen ekosysteemi IMMO-hanketta yhteistyössä Haaga-Helia ammattikorkeakoulun, Helsingin kaupungin ja Laurea-ammattikorkeakoulun kanssa. Tavoitteena on tuottaa IMMO-hankkeen immersiiviseen huonetilaan soveltuva, elämyksellinen ja työelämälähtöinen oppimiskokemus, jonka avulla opiskelijat voivat harjoitella matkailualan tutkinnon osiin ja työelämän osaamistarpeisiin liittyviä tietoja, taitoja ja tilanteita. Ratkaisu voi liittyä yhteen tai useampaan matkailualan osaamisalueeseen. Tarjoajalta ei edellytetä valmista oppimissisältöä tai valmista XR-ratkaisua tarjousvaiheessa, vaan ratkaisun lopulliset sisällöt, oppimistavoitteet ja käyttötapaukset täsmennetään yhteiskehittämisessä. 2. Toimituksen sisältö Hankinta käsittää koko kehitysprosessin suunnittelusta ja konseptoinnista lopulliseen toteutukseen. Toimitukseen sisältyvät vähintään: - vaatimus- ja sisältötyöpajat sekä konseptointi ja käsikirjoitus; - kolme yhteiskehittämistyöpajaa; - oppimis- ja demonstraatioaineistojen rakentaminen; - kehitysversioiden toteuttaminen ja iteratiivinen kehittäminen; - käyttäjätestaukset IMMO-tilassa ja palautteen hyödyntäminen; - ratkaisun viimeistely ja käyttöönottoon liittyvät toimenpiteet; - lähdekoodin, muokattavien lähdetiedostojen, dokumentaation ja muiden sovittujen aineistojen luovuttaminen; ja - loppuraportointi ja avoimen julkaisemisen valmistelu. Yhteiskehittämiseen osallistuu matkailualan opiskelijoita, opettajia, yritysten edustajia ja hankkeen asiantuntijoita. Toimittaja vastaa tarvitsemastaan kehitys- ja testiympäristöstä. Sopimusvelvoitteet suoritetaan EU/ETA-alueella. Toimittajalla on oikeus toteuttaa Ratkaisun suunnittelu, sisällöntuotanto, kehittäminen, ohjelmointi, dokumentointi ja muut toteutustyöt tilariippumattomasti valitsemassaan tarkoituksenmukaisessa ja tietoturvalliseen työskentelyyn soveltuvassa sijainnissa. title: Special Notice Alternate Design and Delivery Methodologies (ADDM) Candidate Projects
description: 1. Description & Purpose The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Europe District (NAU) is issuing this Special Notice seeking information for acquisition planning purposes as part of its ongoing market research and industry intelligence gathering. 10 U.S.C. �2808a permits transactions other than contracts, grants, or cooperative agreements for facility construction and repair�including planning, design, engineering, prototyping, piloting, and execution. NAU is currently evaluating candidate projects as potential test cases for piloting innovative delivery processes and Alternate Design and Delivery Methodologies (ADDM). These methodologies include Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Design-Build to Budget (DB2B / DBtB), Integrated Design and Construction (IDAC), Construction Manager at Risk (CM@Risk), utilizing Other Transaction Authorities (OTA), evaluated alongside traditional Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) delivery models such as Design-Bid-Build (DBB) and Design-Build. Objectives of this Notice The Government is presenting the basic features, current design status, schedule milestones, funding parameters, and known constraints of three (3) candidate projects. Please note: The Government is not requesting capability assessments, corporate marketing presentations, or expressions of interest in competing for these projects. Rather, NAU is seeking targeted industry perspective and analytical feedback on the following core areas: Fit for ADDM Methodologies: Industry perspectives on which of the identified candidate projects are well-suited for specific ADDM methodologies (e.g., PDB, DBtB/DB2B, use of OTA) and the operational, technical, or contractual reasons supporting that fit. Suitability of Traditional FAR Methodologies: Industry perspectives on whether any of the three candidate projects would be better procured through traditional FAR delivery models (e.g., fully USG-controlled Design-Bid-Build) instead of innovative methodologies. Provide a brief rationale for maintaining traditional delivery. 2. Disclaimer & Market Research Notice Non-Commitment: This notice is published strictly for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), Invitation for Bids (IFB), or any commitment by the U.S. Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. No Reimbursement: The Government will not reimburse any costs incurred by industry participants in reviewing this notice, preparing responses, or submitting feedback. Public Releasability & Proprietary Data: Responses to this notice will be treated as public market research. Responding parties are instructed not to submit proprietary information, trade secrets, or protected technologies. Information gathered may be utilized by NAU to inform future acquisition strategies and solicitation development; however, no procurement decisions will be made solely as a result of this notice. 3. Overview of Candidate Projects The three candidate projects under evaluation by USACE Europe District are summarized below based on internal Project Delivery Team (PDT) assessments and engineering reviews. Candidate Project 1: 572070 - FY29 CAP 100672 AFHC Smith Modernization, Baumholder Project Scope: Construct 48 standard design Army Family Housing (AFH) units at Smith Barracks to replace 96 inadequate AFH units. The project constructs four four-story apartment buildings with 12 three-bedroom apartments each. They will be built to meet all current standards. Each apartment building has a ground level garage and four apartments on each of the other three stories. The apartment building includes elevators, a balcony for each apartment, roller shutters and fly screens on each window and balcony door and parking courts on each side of the building that provide access to the ground-level garages. Project includes parking spaces for visitor parking located within close walking distance to the building. Each level in the apartment building is accessible by both elevator and stairs. This project provides new building systems and components to include electrical and mechanical systems, compliance with applicable force protection and energy conservation requirements, balconies, fire alarms/sprinkler systems, elevators, laundry rooms in each apartment, modern kitchens and bathrooms, new efficient heating, plumbing and electrical systems (110 and 220V), TV/telephone/Internet wiring and distribution, built-in closets, doors, windows and storage room. Project includes exterior infrastructure that ties into the existing main utility lines and roadways. It includes connections to storm drainage lines, neighborhood recreational amenities, trash collection enclosures, electrical, water and sewer utility distribution systems and landscaping. It also includes appropriate radon mitigation measures for the new buildings (i.e. installation of a radon tight layer under the floor slab and a passive radon degassing system under the building). An A-E Task Order contract was awarded in FY26 to complete a planning charrette, design charrette, SOW, technical requirements, and required supporting information. Acquisition Schedule: The designer is working on the concept design, with projected completion December 2026. The project is currently indirect (ABG 1 list) and may shift to direct; the regulatory and permitting path is not yet confirmed. The Correctional Service Canada has a requirement to provide Directed Faith Community Reintegration services in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Areas and the Edmonton area. Faith Community Reintegration Projects (FCRPs) support successful offender reintegration following their release from CSC institutions. Directed Faith Community Reintegration Projects (DFCRPs) are a specialized extension of FCRPs that align with CSC’s public safety mandate by supporting the reintegration of offenders from traditionally underserved faith communities. DFCRPs link offender reintegration goals to the mandates of organizations from traditionally underserved faith communities that are prepared to offer religious and spiritual services to offenders after release. DFCRPs support offender reintegration plans and program goals, by providing a range of services and activities that facilitate the transition and reintegration of individuals back into the community. These projects are designed to meet the unique religious and spiritual needs of specific groups, helping ensure that everyone has access to meaningful support on their reintegration journey. Communities of faith typically offer many diverse, faith-based, pro-social activities to the public that foster a sense of belonging while contributing to spiritual and religious growth. Offender involvement in these activities offers a direct means of addressing and mitigating risk factors linked to reoffending. DFCRPs facilitate and support the unique contribution of faith communities toward a holistic approach to safe and restorative reintegration practices. Objectives: To support successful offender reintegration following release from CSC institutions by: • Developing faith community capacity to engage with offenders; • Building bridges between offenders and their religious and spiritual community groups; • Liaising with parole and justice organizations, and faith communities; • Supporting offender reintegration plans and program goals; and • Assisting offenders to become contributing members of society.
